issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §Lexical Elements / grammar DATE, TIME, DATETIME; §DateTime (valid calendar dates, timezone offset range -14:00..+14:00); official CQL conformance invalid="true" precedent
issues.evidence: fhir4ds/cql/parser/lexer.py:_read_datetime_literal (chars '-T:.+Z' collected greedily) + _validate_datetime_literal (ad-hoc partial checks) silently accept malformed temporal literals: '@2024-01-15.year' -> DateTimeLiteral('2024-01-15.year') (evaluates to garbage string '2024-01-15.year'); '@2024-1-1' and '@2024-01-1' (unpadded, and '@2024-1-1 = @2024-01-01' evaluates True); '@2024-02-30' and '@2019-02-29' round-trip unchanged (invalid calendar dates); '@2024-01-15T10:30:22+99:00' accepted and round-trips (offset beyond +/-14:00); '@2024-01-15T10:30:22+02' accepted (grammar requires hh:mm). Expected: LexerError per CQL grammar shape. Repro: .temp/qa/cql03_spec_2026_08_19/probe3.py
issues.root_cause: fhir4ds/cql/parser/lexer.py:_read_datetime_literal collected any alnum/'-T:.+Z' run greedily and _validate_datetime_literal only did ad-hoc partial checks (no strict shape match, no calendar validation, no offset range/format check, no Time-literal range check), so malformed literals lexed silently into garbage DateTimeLiteral values.
issues.resolution: Rewrote _validate_datetime_literal to strict CQL 1.5 grammar shapes (zero-padded DATE/TIME/DATETIME, optional offset Z|+/-hh:mm in -14:00..+14:00) with full calendar (leap-year) validation via datetime.date. Malformed literals now raise LexerError. Patterns composed by concatenation, not f-strings (f-string mangles regex quantifiers like {2}).

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §Equal (Quantity): 'Attempting to operate on quantities with invalid units will result in a null'; §Equivalent: never null for non-null operands
issues.evidence: "5 'xyz' = 5 'xyz'": native C++ returns True, Python fallback returns null (spec: null, invalid unit). "5 'xyz' = 6 'xyz'": C++ False vs py null. "5 'xyz' ~ 5 'xyz'": C++ True vs py False (spec: False). Root cause: extensions/cql/src/cql/quantity.cpp:487 quantity_compare() same-code branch compares values without validating the unit via is_valid_quantity_unit(); unknown UCUM units fall through to value comparison. Repro: .temp/qa/cql03_spec_2026_08_19/probe3.py (DIFF rows)
issues.root_cause: extensions/cql/src/cql/quantity.cpp:quantity_compare() same-unit fast path compared values without validating the unit, so unknown UCUM units compared by value instead of returning null (CQL 1.5 §Equal: invalid units -> null).
issues.resolution: Added same_code_unit_valid_for_compare() guard in extensions/cql/src/cql/quantity.cpp quantity_compare() same-code branch: identical unit codes compare by value only when the unit is valid — a table/calendar/'1' unit, a UCUM annotation ('{dose}', '[pH]'), an annotated known unit ('mm[Hg]'), or a compound of valid components ('mg/m2'). Genuinely unknown codes ('xyz') return null per CQL 1.5 §Equal; equivalence wrapper converts null to false per §Equivalent. First guard version (table-only) regressed 3 DQM measures (CMS69/CMS771/CMS1218 use '{...}', 'mg/m2', '[pH]' units); caught by the PROC_VALIDATION baseline gate and corrected to the annotation/compound-aware validity before closing. Native extension rebuilt (md5 67c1b10a93db5cc47b26082dfc43de21) and deployed to repo bundle + site-packages; md5-verified. Full conformance after fix: 2832/2832 (baseline restored).

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 §ToString (Quantity/Ratio overloads): string representation examples '5 mg', '0.1 mg':0.1 mg'
issues.evidence: ToString(5 'mg') -> "5 'mg'" (drops decimal) but ToString(1:8) -> "1.0 '1':8.0 '1'" (keeps decimal). Value formatting inconsistent between Quantity and Ratio paths; spec examples never show a trailing .0 for whole Decimal values. Repro: probe2.py
issues.root_cause: Deliberate Decimal-semantics formatting: Ratio values are Decimals so RatioToString renders '1.0' (test_ratio_udfs.py pins '10.0 mg:2.0 mL'); QuantityToString macro strips trailing '.0'. Both backends agree; spec examples never exercise whole-value Ratio formatting.
issues.resolution: No change; documented in AGENTS.md NOT A BUG Registry.
